As a Ukrainian player, I was automatically assigned to the Russian region upon launching the game for the first time. The servers, text language, and audio were all set to Russian with no option to change this during setup.

For Ukrainian users being placed into the Russian region feels dismissive and disrespectful. Ukraine has its own distinct identity, language, and culture, and many Ukrainians are very sensitive about this kind of automatic grouping.

I'd encourage the developers and Steam to consider:
- Assigning Ukrainian accounts to the European region by default
- Making language and server selection clearly available during first launch
- Ideally, adding Ukrainian language support

I genuinely want to enjoy this game, and I hope these concerns are taken seriously. Thank you for reading.

I've gotten to level 20 now, and I have to say. I'm kind of impressed. I'll review some of the game I've found stunning.

My first praise for this game is its graphics. Everything looks beautiful. And even with all these stunning graphics, my computer is handling it surprisingly well. I thought I'd be experiencing frame drops every few seconds on low quality (my computer isn't the greatest so I'm used to it). But I play on high quality and still have at least 40fps constantly. The world is beautiful and I'm able to experience it without many frame drops.

My second praise is the combat system. First of all, combat in these graphics look amazing. Secondly, the combat feels smooth and fun. There are a variety of abilities you can use in combat. I checked my skill list and I saw much more abilities than I've ever seen in any other games that I've played. Combat in this game is just amazing.

It's not perfect however. As a new player, I had an information overload when looking through everything. It took me a while, but I played around with what I could do and got a decent idea of what they were. If it's your first time playing the game, don't expect to jump in knowing how to do everything, or even expecting an npc or a guide to tell you everything. It's all in front of you. You just need to figure out how it works.

This game is life-skilling with a side of MMORPG. Lots of crafting and harvesting to be expected. If you are solely looking for a combat-only focused MMO, this game is not for you. This is because progress for each aspect of the game can slow drastically, so its best to dip your hand in many pots.

Most 'playtime' on player's profiles is AFK hours while fishing in-game, one of the lifeskilling things that has the most profit. In order to reach endgame content, the majority of your playtime will likely being leaving your computer running while your character fishes or trains horses.

The content is very confusing and vast, requiring guides in nearly every step of the way. You will not find success without them, but there is plenty of helpful content online.

The player-based economy is very well done, featuring the 'Central Market', a shop where players buy and sell items they earn through missions, crafting, harvesting, or enemy drops.

It will take a large investment of time to understand the even larger amount of mechanics and progression. But if you're willing to sink time into this MMO, there's plenty to enjoy.

The game and it's launcher will be in Turkish, you have to change them separately.
For the launcher you need to go to the top right and click the settings cogwheel icon and select EN-US and then click Tamam (which i think means accept?)
after that the launcher will be in English after you restart it.

The game itself will still be in Turkish and you'll need to navigate to the settings panel by clicking the button that says "Ayarlar" the next part is extremely easy, under "Dil Ayari" select "Ingilizce" then at the bottom click "Uygula" to apply the change, the game then tells you to restart in Turkish. You can quit the game by clicking on the "Onayla" button and then clicking the middle button on the main menu which says "Cik" and a prompt will come up, press "Evet"
